```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Setup: load dummy data for template preview.
# In production, this is replaced with real data loading from
# pntmoni-pipeline output (Parquet on local or GCS).

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl
from matplotlib.patches import Polygon
from matplotlib.collections import PatchCollection

# PNT Moni data-palette colors — source of truth is
# pntmoni-docs/60-brand/tokens.json (ADR 0017). Figures use the DATA
# palette only; brand gold #E8C438 must never appear in figure code.
COLOR_PRIMARY = "#2E6DA8"   # data blue — chart primary
COLOR_SECONDARY = "#22273A" # brand ink — axis labels / reference lines
COLOR_EMPHASIS = "#16406E"  # data emphasis — trend endpoints / deep blue
COLOR_SUCCESS = "#2E8B6B"   # status normal — positive/normal deltas
COLOR_WARNING = "#E08A1E"   # status degraded
COLOR_DANGER = "#C24B3A"    # status critical
COLOR_NEUTRAL = "#6B7384"   # muted neutral (brand text.muted)
COLOR_INSIDE = "#2E6DA8"   # 網内 — data primary
COLOR_OUTSIDE = "#6B7384"  # 網外 — muted neutral (semantic contrast kept)

# Perceptually-uniform continuous colormap (matplotlib "plasma") for the
# magnitude heatmaps, matching the Free-tier spatial maps: perceptually
# ordered, colorblind-safe, no green/red good–bad coding — the per-station
# maps read as error magnitude, not a pass/fail verdict (PS-QZSS
# reference-value convention). Progression: purple (smaller) → yellow
# (larger). Colour limits stay percentile-clipped per map (5th–95th) so
# station-level outliers remain legible.
CMAP_SEQUENTIAL = plt.cm.plasma

mpl.rcParams['axes.spines.top'] = False
mpl.rcParams['axes.spines.right'] = False
mpl.rcParams['axes.grid'] = True
mpl.rcParams['grid.alpha'] = 0.3
mpl.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 100
# CJK font support — figure labels carry a few Japanese tokens (網内 /
# 網外). The matplotlib default (DejaVu Sans) has no JP glyphs, so they
# render as tofu boxes in HTML and PDF alike. Prefer macOS Hiragino, then
# Yu Gothic, then Noto CJK on Linux.
mpl.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = [
    'IBM Plex Sans JP', 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Hiragino Sans',
    'Hiragino Maru Gothic Pro', 'Yu Gothic', 'Noto Sans CJK JP',
    'DejaVu Sans',
]
mpl.rcParams['font.family'] = 'sans-serif'
mpl.rcParams['axes.unicode_minus'] = False
# Embed fonts as TrueType (type 42), NOT Type 3. The default Type-3 PDF
# path ASCII-encodes a per-glyph XObject name; CJK glyph names (Hiragino)
# are non-ASCII and raise UnicodeEncodeError, killing a `--to pdf` render
# on the first figure with Japanese text. Type 42 embeds the subsetted
# TrueType font and addresses glyphs by id, avoiding the ASCII-name encode.
mpl.rcParams['pdf.fonttype'] = 42
mpl.rcParams['ps.fonttype'] = 42

# ---- Derived from the parameters cell ----
# YEAR / MONTH / PERIOD / STREAM / MODE / version strings / CONFIG_HASH /
# DATA_MODE / INPUTS / INPUTS_STATUS are all defined in the papermill
# ``parameters`` cell above (and overridden at production render time).
PERIOD_LABEL = pd.Timestamp(int(YEAR), int(MONTH), 1).strftime("%B %Y")

# ---- Synthetic data generation ----
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)
N_STATIONS = 1300
N_SAMPLES_PER_STATION = 200

# Synthetic station identifiers and geographic distribution
# Coordinates roughly cover the Japanese archipelago
station_ids = [f"{i:04d}" for i in range(N_STATIONS)]
station_lats = rng.uniform(30.5, 45.5, N_STATIONS)
station_lons = rng.uniform(129.5, 145.5, N_STATIONS)

# Synthetic per-epoch errors per station (gamma-distributed)
horiz_errors = rng.gamma(2.0, 0.025, size=(N_STATIONS, N_SAMPLES_PER_STATION))
vert_errors = rng.gamma(2.0, 0.040, size=(N_STATIONS, N_SAMPLES_PER_STATION))

# 80% inside-network, 20% outside-network (synthetic)
inside_network = rng.choice([True, False], size=N_STATIONS, p=[0.80, 0.20])

# TTFF samples
ttff_15min = rng.gamma(2.5, 12, size=12000)

# All-station aggregated quantiles
all_horiz = horiz_errors.flatten()
all_vert = vert_errors.flatten()

H50 = np.quantile(all_horiz, 0.50)
H95 = np.quantile(all_horiz, 0.95)
H99 = np.quantile(all_horiz, 0.99)
V50 = np.quantile(all_vert, 0.50)
V95 = np.quantile(all_vert, 0.95)
V99 = np.quantile(all_vert, 0.99)
TTFF50 = np.quantile(ttff_15min, 0.50)
TTFF95 = np.quantile(ttff_15min, 0.95)
AVAIL = 0.987  # synthetic national availability

# Per-station 95th percentile (for heatmaps)
station_h95 = np.array([np.quantile(horiz_errors[i], 0.95) for i in range(N_STATIONS)])
station_v95 = np.array([np.quantile(vert_errors[i], 0.95) for i in range(N_STATIONS)])

# Inside vs Outside network statistics
inside_h95 = np.quantile(horiz_errors[inside_network].flatten(), 0.95)
outside_h95 = np.quantile(horiz_errors[~inside_network].flatten(), 0.95)
inside_v95 = np.quantile(vert_errors[inside_network].flatten(), 0.95)
outside_v95 = np.quantile(vert_errors[~inside_network].flatten(), 0.95)

# ---- Synthetic past 13 months of monthly aggregates ----
# Phase 0 ADR 0007 scope: Apr 2025 onwards. Phase 0 launch in mid-2026
# means ~13+ months of history is available at first publication.
months_back = 13
trend_months = []
trend_h95 = []
trend_v95 = []
for i in range(months_back, 0, -1):
    target = pd.Timestamp(YEAR, MONTH, 1) - pd.DateOffset(months=i-1)
    trend_months.append(target.strftime("%Y-%m"))
    seasonal = 0.005 * np.sin((target.month - 4) * np.pi / 6)
    trend_h95.append(0.045 + seasonal + rng.normal(0, 0.0015))
    trend_v95.append(0.080 + 1.5 * seasonal + rng.normal(0, 0.0025))
trend_h95 = np.array(trend_h95)
trend_v95 = np.array(trend_v95)

# Mark current month, last 6 months, year-ago month
current_idx = len(trend_months) - 1
last6_start_idx = max(0, current_idx - 5)
yago_idx = max(0, current_idx - 12)

# ---- Synthetic CLAS evaluation network grid ----
# In production, this is replaced with the actual CLAS network
# definition. Here we use a simple polygon roughly enclosing the
# core Japan archipelago for visualization.
NETWORK_POLYGON = np.array([
    [129.5, 31.0], [131.0, 30.7], [131.5, 32.5], [134.0, 33.5],
    [136.5, 34.0], [138.5, 34.5], [140.5, 35.5], [141.5, 38.5],
    [142.0, 41.0], [141.5, 43.0], [140.0, 44.5], [137.5, 44.5],
    [136.0, 43.0], [133.0, 38.0], [131.0, 35.5], [130.0, 33.5],
    [129.5, 31.0]
])
```

# Introduction

This report covers QZSS CLAS (Centimeter Level Augmentation Service)
performance during **`{python} PERIOD_LABEL`**, evaluated by PNT Moni
using publicly-available data and open-source tools.

PNT Moni is an independent evaluation service for GNSS augmentation,
providing continuous monitoring of CLAS performance at higher spatial
and temporal resolution than the official Cabinet Office of Japan / QSS
Performance Reports. PNT Moni's monthly reports complement the
semi-annual official reports through monthly granularity, station-level
drill-down, and analytical depth that addresses the practical needs of
receiver manufacturers, system integrators, and CLAS-using operators.

The methodology used to produce this report is summarized in the next
section. Full methodology documentation is at
[https://pntmoni.com/methodology/v1.0.1](https://pntmoni.com/methodology/v1.0.1).
The Methodology Version Tag at the end of this report uniquely
identifies the configuration used.

# Methodology

This section provides a summary of the methodology. The full
methodology document is at the link above.

**Data sources**: GEONET 30-second RINEX observations from
approximately 1,300 stations, distributed by the Geospatial Information
Authority of Japan (GSI) under PDL 1.0
(出典：国土地理院 電子基準点データ提供サービス).
QSS L6 broadcast archive from Cabinet Office of Japan. IGS final SP3/CLK
products for validation.

**Processing engine**: `{python} f"{ENGINE} {ENGINE_VERSION}"` operating in
kinematic PPP-RTK mode with per-system clock parameterization and
RAIM/FDE. See [ADR 0001](../../../pntmoni-docs/70-decisions/adr-0001.md)
and [ADR 0004](../../../pntmoni-docs/70-decisions/adr-0004.md).

**Reference coordinate derivation**: GSI F3 daily solutions (ITRF2005)
prior to August 2021; F5 daily solutions (ITRF2014) from August 2021
onwards. A 2-week median filter suppresses coordinate spikes
(methodology following Shiono & Kubo 2026, NAVIGATION).

**Quality control**: `{python} f"{QC_TOOL} {QC_VERSION}"`
during 2026–2027 (transitioning to mrtk qc at 2027/Q4 per
[ADR 0008](../../../pntmoni-docs/70-decisions/adr-0008.md)).

**Statistical aggregation**: 95th and 99th percentile errors computed
per station and aggregated nationally. TTFF measured with **15-minute
reset period** (NAVIGATION 2026 continuity); 60-minute reset added in
Phase 1. See [ADR 0005](../../../pntmoni-docs/70-decisions/adr-0005.md).

**Known structural divergence from QSS official numbers**: PNT Moni's
methodology differs from the official QSS Performance Report in four
documented ways: sampling rate (30s vs 1s), parameter settings re-tuned
for 30s sampling, CLASLIB version lag, and consequent Kalman filter
behavior. See [ADR 0001 Postscript](../../../pntmoni-docs/70-decisions/adr-0001.md#postscript)
and [Shiono & Kubo (2025, 2026)](https://doi.org/10.33012/navi.762).
This is documented as a structural property, not an error.

## Evaluation Network

Stations are classified as **inside-network (網内)** or
**outside-network (網外)** based on the official CLAS coverage
definition. The network polygon below is updated only when the CLAS
operational coverage changes (rare); the version of the polygon is
encoded in the methodology version tag at the end of this report.

```{python}
#| label: fig-network-map
#| fig-cap: "Evaluation network coverage and station distribution"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 7))

# Background: rough Japan outline (very simple coastline approximation)
# In production, replace with proper basemap or shapefile
ax.set_xlim(127, 147)
ax.set_ylim(28, 47)
ax.set_aspect("equal")

# Network polygon (filled)
network_patch = Polygon(NETWORK_POLYGON, closed=True,
                         facecolor=COLOR_PRIMARY, alpha=0.10,
                         edgecolor=COLOR_PRIMARY, linewidth=1.5,
                         linestyle="--", label="CLAS network coverage")
ax.add_patch(network_patch)

# Station points: inside (data blue) and outside (muted neutral)
ax.scatter(station_lons[inside_network], station_lats[inside_network],
           c=COLOR_INSIDE, s=6, alpha=0.6, label=f"網内 (n={int(inside_network.sum())})")
ax.scatter(station_lons[~inside_network], station_lats[~inside_network],
           c=COLOR_OUTSIDE, s=6, alpha=0.7, label=f"網外 (n={int((~inside_network).sum())})")

ax.set_xlabel("Longitude (°E)")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9, framealpha=0.95)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
```

The network polygon defines the area within which CLAS is intended to
deliver specified performance. Stations outside this area receive
corrections derived through extrapolation, with potentially different
error characteristics analyzed in §5.3.1.

# Performance

## National Overview

### Distribution of errors

```{python}
#| label: fig-horiz-cdf
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative distribution of horizontal error across all stations"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
sorted_h = np.sort(all_horiz)
cdf = np.arange(1, len(sorted_h) + 1) / len(sorted_h)
ax.plot(sorted_h * 100, cdf, color=COLOR_PRIMARY, linewidth=2)

for q, label in [(0.50, "50%"), (0.95, "95%"), (0.99, "99%")]:
    v = np.quantile(all_horiz, q) * 100
    ax.axvline(v, linestyle="--", color=COLOR_SECONDARY, alpha=0.4)
    ax.annotate(f"{label} = {v:.2f} cm", xy=(v, q), xytext=(v + 1, q - 0.05),
                fontsize=8, alpha=0.7)

ax.set_xlabel("Horizontal error (cm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative probability")
ax.set_xlim(0, max(sorted_h) * 100 * 0.6)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ttff-15min
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of TTFF (15-minute reset period)"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.hist(ttff_15min, bins=60, color=COLOR_PRIMARY, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white")
for q, label, c in [(0.50, "50%", COLOR_SECONDARY),
                     (0.95, "95%", COLOR_WARNING)]:
    v = np.quantile(ttff_15min, q)
    ax.axvline(v, linestyle="--", color=c, label=f"{label} = {v:.1f} s")
ax.set_xlabel("TTFF (seconds)")
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Detailed Analysis

### Inside/Outside Network Analysis

The CLAS evaluation network defines a coverage area within which
correction quality is intended to meet specification. Stations
outside this network ("網外") receive corrections derived through
extrapolation, with potentially different performance characteristics.

PNT Moni distinguishes inside-network (網内) and outside-network (網外)
stations using the official CLAS coverage definition (see §3.1
Evaluation Network for the spatial visualization). The following
analysis quantifies the performance gap.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-inside-outside
#| tbl-cap: "Inside vs Outside Network performance (synthetic)"

io_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Group": ["網内 (Inside)", "網外 (Outside)"],
    "Stations": [int(inside_network.sum()), int((~inside_network).sum())],
    "H 95% (cm)": [f"{inside_h95*100:.2f}", f"{outside_h95*100:.2f}"],
    "V 95% (cm)": [f"{inside_v95*100:.2f}", f"{outside_v95*100:.2f}"],
})
io_table
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-inside-outside-cdf
#| fig-cap: "CDF comparison: inside vs outside network"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
inside_h = horiz_errors[inside_network].flatten()
outside_h = horiz_errors[~inside_network].flatten()

for label, data, color in [
    ("網内 (Inside)", inside_h, COLOR_INSIDE),
    ("網外 (Outside)", outside_h, COLOR_OUTSIDE),
]:
    sorted_d = np.sort(data)
    cdf = np.arange(1, len(sorted_d) + 1) / len(sorted_d)
    ax.plot(sorted_d * 100, cdf, color=color, linewidth=2, label=label)

ax.set_xlabel("Horizontal error (cm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative probability")
ax.set_xlim(0, max(np.max(inside_h), np.max(outside_h)) * 100 * 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
```

The performance gap between inside and outside network at the 95th
percentile is **`{python} f"{(outside_h95 - inside_h95)*100:.2f} cm"`**
horizontal. This gap is monitored over time and discussed in the
context of CLAS network design considerations
(see Shiono & Kubo 2026 NAVIGATION for foundational analysis).

Kobe, Tsukuba) which may switch during operations. Switching events
are detected from the broadcast metadata and reported here as a
context indicator for any short-term changes in correction
characteristics.

## Anomalies

### Alert flags

L6 broadcast alert messages are flags transmitted within the CLAS
correction stream indicating known issues at the source (CSSR
generation level). These are tracked monthly to give subscribers
visibility into the broadcast's self-reported health.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if not L6_ALERTS_PRESENT:
    print(
        f"For **{PERIOD_LABEL}**: L6 alert aggregation has not been "
        f"produced for this period — run "
        f"`pntmoni-pipeline analyze l6-alerts --period {PERIOD}` "
        f"to populate (methodology §6)."
    )
elif N_L6_ALERTS == 0:
    print(
        f"For **{PERIOD_LABEL}**: **0 alert messages detected** across "
        f"the L6 broadcast (no alert flags raised)."
    )
else:
    _per_prn = ", ".join(f"PRN {p}: {c}" for p, c in sorted(L6_ALERTS_PER_PRN.items()))
    print(
        f"For **{PERIOD_LABEL}**: **{N_L6_ALERTS} alert message(s) "
        f"detected** across the L6 broadcast ({_per_prn})."
    )
```

### Divergences (Tropospheric)

PNT Moni detects tropospheric divergence events—periods when CLAS
troposphere correction values deviate physically from expected
values, leading to performance degradation. This is the most common
class of CLAS broadcast anomaly and a critical monitoring function
for users.

Detection methodology combines a statistical threshold (rolling
distribution-based) with an absolute threshold (physical magnitude
of divergence). Events are reported when both conditions are
satisfied for sustained periods.

For `{python} PERIOD_LABEL`: **0 tropospheric divergence events
detected.** Detailed methodology will be documented in
`30-evaluation-methodology/07-anomaly-detection.md`.
